newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Ecopetrol to issue oil-backed debt.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Ecopetrol to issue oil-backed debt.

text.p: Colombia's state oil company, Ecopetrol, said it would actively begin seeking a foreign investment bank next week to help finance its investment program through the sale of oil-backed securities or other financial instruments aboard.

Felix Betancourt, Ecopetrol's vice president in charge of finance, said the bank selected for the asset-backed securitization plan, the first of its kind in Colombia, would be responsible for setting up a trust to which Ecopetrol would cede its rights to a small portion of Colombia's oil output.

The trust would then issue bonds or other instruments, or arrange syndicated loans, backed by the oil under its control, to come up with $150 million to help finance development of Colombia's huge Cusiana and Cupiaqua oil fields, Betancourt said. "They (the investment bank) will be responsible for raising the money," Bentancourt told Reuters in a telephone interview.

He said Ecopetrol would initially cede its rights to 10,000 barrels of the oil produced daily by Cusiana and Cupiagua, but he did not specify the timeframe during which the oil would be held as collateral.

Betancourt said Ecopetrol hoped to interest an investment bank with a strong presence in the United States, Japan and Europe in the securitization plan but he did not identify any prospects by name, saying only that formal invitiations to a select group of banks would be issued next week.
